marker_divergence — DRIVE tactorque op

• Data kinds: matrix × matrix × scalar → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.marker_divergence(pts, u, radius: 'float', min_neighbors: 'int' = 4, k_max: 'int' = 24) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import tactorque; tactorque.marker_divergence(pts, u, radius: 'float', min_neighbors: 'int' = 4, k_max: 'int' = 24) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("marker_divergence"))

Usage

Per-point divergence div = ∂ux/∂x + ∂uy/∂y and curl curl = ∂uy/∂x − ∂ux/∂y from scattered markers pts (N, 2) and displacements u (N, 2) (unit = unit of u ÷ unit of pts). Fits a plane c0 + c1 x + c2 y by least squares to the points within the neighborhood radius radius (at most k_max points) (on a regular grid with a radius of 1.01 pitch this equals the 5-point central difference and agrees with sceneflow.flow_divergence to 1e-15; with a radius of 1.5 pitch the 9 points give a row-averaged difference that differs by 11 % at the border, measured). Solves the normal equations for all points in one batch. Points with fewer than min_neighbors neighbors or with singular (collinear) normal equations get valid = False and div/curl = nan (fail-closed: never silently 0). The same op works for scattered FEM nodes. Raises ValueError: pts/u is not (N, 2), shapes differ, radius ≤ 0, N < min_neighbors.
